learningObjectives: Parameterize an oriented interval by endpoints and by midpoint plus half-opening angle.
Explain precisely how an interval or geodesic becomes a point of a derived kinematic space.
Identify degeneracy, orientation, branch, and quotient issues in the parameterization.
Keep the AdS3/CFT2 hypotheses separate from a general relational analogy.
definitions: Oriented interval: an interval whose ordered endpoints retain an orientation.
Kinematic point: one element of a derived space representing an interval or geodesic.
Midpoint coordinate: the average of lifted endpoint coordinates.
Half-opening angle: half the endpoint separation on the chosen lift.
Degenerate interval: the limiting case in which the endpoints coincide.
Branch data: additional identity needed when the same endpoints admit multiple relevant geodesics or phases.
notebookPrompt: Create a mathematically serious cinematic lesson titled ‘From intervals to points.’ In the explicitly labeled AdS3/CFT2 setting, animate ordered endpoint pairs (u,v) on a boundary circle, the associated boundary interval and bulk geodesic, and then map each whole object to one point in a second kinematic space. Reparameterize using midpoint θ=(u+v)/2 and half-opening angle α=(v-u)/2; show θ moving the interval and α changing its size. Treat α→0 as a domain boundary or degeneracy. Preserve orientation and show how multiple-geodesic or phase-transition branches can defeat a naive endpoint-only label. Include the negative control that becoming a kinematic point does not make the interval dimensionless in its original space. State all holographic and semiclassical hypotheses and use no unsupported universalization.
humanFrame: The central conceptual move is a change of ontology between spaces: extended objects in one space can be elementary points in another. Every visual transition must keep the two spaces visibly distinct.
assessment: Convert three endpoint pairs into midpoint/opening coordinates, identify the degenerate limit, explain the role of orientation, and give one case where endpoint labels require additional branch data.
